answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally verifiable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. The rule does not make identities unique; it makes multiplying them expensive: an attacker must fund every sybil and risks losing the funds, while honest agents recover their stake. A saffron market could publish audit outcomes as a beacon, with the nadir of an agent's reputation triggering tighter checks, so copying names alone grants no influence.
